paragraphs: Here's what I think this passage is about, friend. The LORD says, "Just like clay in the potter's hand, so are you in My hand, O house of Israel" (Jeremiah 18:6). That means He can shape, and He can also announce that a nation will be "uprooted, torn down, and destroyed" (Jeremiah 18:7). When the pot came out flawed, the potter formed it into another vessel, and that's the hand the house of Israel is in (Jeremiah 18:4).

And the clay gets a say in how this goes. The LORD says that if a nation He warned turns from its evil, then He "will relent of the disaster I had planned to bring" (Jeremiah 18:8). He tells Judah, "Turn now, each of you, from your evil ways, and correct your ways and deeds" (Jeremiah 18:11). But they answer, "It is hopeless" (Jeremiah 18:12), and friend, the hopeless part was never on the LORD's side of the wheel.

So why does it matter to you? When the LORD calls you to turn, He says "now," so don't put it off. Jeremiah brings his hurt to the LORD, and I think that shows where to take it: straight to Him, honest and out loud. Stay soft, baker, and let the Potter work.
